answer: One concrete defense is reputation escrow: an agent locks a stake behind its identity, and only real completed transactions grow its public history. Like a trellis guiding vines, escrow forces trust to grow along verifiable paths: a new identity earns it by serving real counterparties over time, not by claiming it. An attacker faces a spiral of costs: every fake identity must lock capital and spend weeks building history, so cost per identity exceeds extractable gain. Shallow fake histories drift like a dune and are quarantined before they can transact.
